question: What will the first reported revenues after October 2026 be for Snowflake?

calls.reasoning: Q3 FY27 product revenue guide $1,588-1,593M; PS&other ~$55M (Q1 56.6, Q2 54.9), so guide-implied total ~$1,645M. Product beats vs guide midpoint over the last 6 quarters ran +2.7% to +5.5% (last two +5.5%, +5.2%), implying total ~$1,688-1,733M. But this guide is less conservative (37-38% y/y vs prior actual 37%, where earlier guides sat 1-7 pts below), and historical Q2->Q3 sequential growth (6.4-8.6%) points to ~$1,666-1,696M. Consensus product ~$1,619M, Morgan Stanley $1,640M on positive checks. Center ~$1,700M total, SD ~$28-30M. Polymarket: thin (~$1.6K volume) 'Q3 product revenue >$1.58B' at 89% - different metric/threshold, evidence only; no total-revenue market and no Kalshi contract found.
calls.reference_class: Snowflake quarterly product revenue vs guidance midpoint, last 6 quarters (FY26 Q1 - FY27 Q2), plus PS&other run-rate

calls.reasoning: Q3 FY27 product revenue guide $1,588-1,593M (midpoint 1,590.5) plus ~$55M professional services gives ~$1,645M total at guide. Over the last 10 quarters, product revenue beat the guide midpoint by 2.4-5.6% (mean ~4.3%; last two 5.5% and 5.2%). A 5.0% beat is the line between the 1,670-1,725 and >1,725 bins, so the split is close to a coin flip. If Q2's in-quarter growth (~3.8%/month) continued, product revenue would be ~$1,668M, about $1,723M total. Morgan Stanley estimates $1.64B product (~$1,695M total). Median total ~ $1,718M. No human prediction market found (Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold searched); an unattributed '84% >$1.62B product' claim was not used as an anchor.
